values: Prévenir que introduces the information communicated; when naming the person warned, use prévenir quelqu’un que or prévenir quelqu’un de quelque chose.
Quel agrees in gender and number with the noun it determines and remains separate from que: quelle que soit la raison, quels que soient les résultats.
Introduces a consequence, risk, or concession the subject is prepared to accept in pursuing the main action.
Written as two words when it means whatever; it introduces a subjunctive clause and must not be confused with quoique meaning although.
Written as one word when it means although; it introduces a concession and requires the subjunctive.
Used for visiting a person and requires à; visiting a place normally uses visiter directly.
Renoncer requires à before the thing abandoned and can also be followed by an infinitive.
Réussir à un examen means to pass it successfully; passer un examen means to sit or take it, without stating the result.
Rêver de commonly refers either to dreaming during sleep or to strongly desiring a person, thing, or situation.
Rêver à means to let one’s thoughts dwell on something and is less common than rêver de in everyday usage.

batch_summary: Added orthographic and mood distinctions for quel que, quoi que, and quoique, plus construction guidance for visit, exam, warning, and dreaming expressions.
